title: Algorithm Problems: Part 2
summary: Track more than one piece of state and handle **edge cases** first.
refresher: A multi-step algorithm may remember a best **value** and where it appeared. Write the rule that should remain true after every **loop** pass, decide what happens for empty **input** and ties, then trace a small example.

sections.title: Track related facts
sections.summary: Keep the saved value and index rule visible while looping.

blocks.body: A harder algorithm often remembers several related facts. To find the position of the largest **value**, remember the best position found so far and compare every later value with it. Decide the empty-**input** result before reading position zero.

blocks.title: Track best-so-far state
blocks.caption: Trace the invariant from edge-case guard to final returned index.

steps.title: Guard empty input
steps.body: Before using index 0, decide what the algorithm returns for an empty input.

state.note: The edge case is handled before reading a first item.

steps.title: Initialize invariant
steps.body: Use the first item as the first best candidate, then state what best means.

state.note: Invariant: best is the index of the largest checked value.

steps.title: Update when better
steps.body: Compare index 1 with the saved best. Since 9 is larger than 4, best must move.

state.note: The saved index and saved meaning stay in sync.

steps.title: Keep when not better
steps.body: Compare index 2 with best. Since 7 is not larger than 9, the invariant says best stays put.

state.note: Not every pass updates the saved state.

steps.title: Return the tracked fact
steps.body: After the loop, return the fact the variable promised to track: the best index.

state.note: The trace reaches the final returned index.

blocks.body: A rule that stays true after every **loop** pass is called an invariant. Here the rule is simple: after checking through position `i`, `best` stores the position of the largest **value** seen so far. Writing that sentence first makes the update easier to verify.

blocks.title: The algorithm is not C++-specific
blocks.body: You would keep the same best-so-far rule in Python. C++ adds explicit vector and **index** types, but the reasoning and the small hand trace are identical.

sections.title: Candidate and edge case
sections.summary: Handle empty input before using the first element as a candidate.

blocks.caption: The empty case is handled before position zero is used. Each larger **value** replaces the saved best position.
Handle empty **input** before creating an element-based candidate.

blocks.body: For `{4, 9, 7}`, `best` starts at zero, changes to one after nine, and stays one after seven. Using `>` keeps the first position when two maximum **values** tie. Using `>=` would keep the last tied position.

sections.title: Tie and empty checks
sections.summary: Trace tie behavior and empty-input safety before coding.

blocks.title: Handle empty input before choosing a candidate
blocks.body: Position zero is a valid starting candidate only when the vector contains an element. Check `.empty()` before reading or comparing any element.

blocks.why: The first element already supplies the current candidate, so only later positions need comparison.
An equal later **value** does not satisfy greater-than, preserving the earlier **index**.

sections.title: Algorithm Part 2 checklist
sections.summary: Review the habits for multi-step C++ algorithms.

algo-p2-01.title: Sorted flag invariant
algo-p2-01.body: This algorithm keeps a flag that means no out-of-order pair has been found yet. Each pass compares a value with the value just before it.
algo-p2-01.notice: The loop starts after the first item because each comparison looks backward one position.
algo-p2-01.mistake: Do not compare a value with itself or start at a position with no previous neighbor.

algo-p2-02.title: Running totals
algo-p2-02.body: Running totals keep one ongoing total and record a snapshot after each addition. The saved collection grows after the current value is included.
algo-p2-02.notice: Add first, then store the new total for that position.
algo-p2-02.mistake: Do not reset the total each pass; only the snapshot changes each pass.

algo-p2-03.title: Nested matrix scan
algo-p2-03.body: A matrix count needs two loops: one to choose each row and one to inspect each value in that row. The counter changes only on a target match.
algo-p2-03.notice: The inner loop must be nested inside the row loop.
algo-p2-03.mistake: Do not increment once per row when the prompt asks for matching cells.

algo-p2-04.title: Two best values
algo-p2-04.body: Tracking the largest and second-largest distinct values means the variables depend on each other. When a new largest appears, the old largest has to move into second place.
algo-p2-04.notice: Update second before replacing largest with the new value.
algo-p2-04.mistake: Do not let a duplicate of the largest count as the second-largest distinct value.

algo-p2-05.title: First occurrences
algo-p2-05.body: This pattern preserves order by scanning left to right and adding a value only if it has not already been kept.
algo-p2-05.notice: The membership check happens before the append or add step.
algo-p2-05.mistake: Do not sort the values or use a plain set if the prompt asks to keep first-seen order.

algo-p2-06.title: Mirrored string positions
algo-p2-06.body: A palindrome check compares matching positions from the front and back. One mismatch is enough to change the answer flag.
algo-p2-06.notice: Only half the string needs direct comparisons.
algo-p2-06.mistake: Do not compare every character with the same final character.

algo-p2-07.title: Reset row-local state
algo-p2-07.body: A best-row algorithm has two levels of state: a row total that restarts for each row and a best value that survives across rows.
algo-p2-07.notice: Reset the row total inside the outer loop but before the inner loop.
algo-p2-07.mistake: Do not reset the best value for every row.

algo-p2-08.title: Separate kept values and zeros
algo-p2-08.body: Moving zeros to the end can be traced as two pieces of state: the kept nonzero values and the number of zeros seen so far.
algo-p2-08.notice: The scan preserves nonzero order first, then appends the counted zeros.
algo-p2-08.mistake: Do not append zeros immediately if the prompt wants them all at the end.
